QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_48

question.text: Ms. Sunita Patil moves from limited-assurance to reasonable-assurance on a SAS-400 gender-inclusion engagement. Other things equal, her evidence-collection plan will MOST LIKELY require:

answer.text: A larger sample, more independent corroboration, and wider procedures to reduce assurance risk to an 'acceptably low' rather than 'moderate' level
Dropping beneficiary interviews because they are qualitative
Dropping control-group data because it is redundant

explanation.text: The Logic: Reasonable assurance requires reducing assurance risk to 'acceptably low' (typically implying larger samples, more independent corroboration, additional procedures), vs limited assurance targeting 'moderate'. Qualitative interviews and control-group data become MORE important, not less, when moving up. The Trap: Options B, C, D contradict the assurance-risk logic. Upgrading assurance never means dropping evidence. Cross-Exam Context: III-A / III-C Compliance reference ISAE 3000 assurance risk; XXIII applies the same machinery to SAS-100 engagements. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Quantify the incremental budget cost of moving from limited to reasonable at the engagement-letter stage — a 2-3x cost bump is typical, and it's best flagged BEFORE field work begins, not after.
